html:
French Indo-China in the years between the world wars, shown on the map from 1920 to 1938. Its founding years are under French Indochina.

Rubber boomed in these years. Large plantations in Cochinchina and Cambodia, Michelin's among them, used workers from the north under harsh contracts, and many died. A new Vietnamese class educated in French schools wrote in the Vietnamese alphabet, and new faiths such as Caodaism drew large followings.

Nationalism hardened. The Yên Bái mutiny of 1930 failed and its leaders were executed. The same year Hồ Chí Minh founded the Indochinese Communist Party. Peasant uprisings in 1930 and 1931 were crushed, and the Great Depression hit rice and rubber prices hard.

Japan moved troops in from 1940 and ousted the French in March 1945. The famine of 1945 followed. France fought to return in the First Indochina War, which ended with its defeat at Điện Biên Phủ in 1954.
